title: Veterans Wanted: Drive Big Rigs as Immigrant Truckers Lose Licenses
summary: Have you ever seen a huge 18-wheeler on the highway and wondered who's driving? Soon, it might be more U.S. military veterans. The government just launched a campaign called 'Freedom Haulers' to get veterans into trucking jobs. Why? Because tens of thousands of immigrant truck drivers have lost their licenses this year. It all started last summer when the Transportation Department began checking if truckers could speak English, which is a rule. Then, after a bad crash in Florida where an immigrant driver made an illegal U-turn and three people died, they cracked down even harder. Audits found many licenses were given out illegally or stayed valid after work permits expired. So far, about 26,000 drivers were pulled off the road for failing English tests, and 30,000 licenses were canceled. Now, the government wants veterans to fill those empty seats. Here's the cool part: if you drove big military vehicles (over 2.5 tons) recently, you can skip the skills test for a commercial driver's license. Others can go to trucking school during their last six months of service, and the GI Bill pays 100% of the cost — even a housing allowance! More than 40,000 vets have already used this fast-track program. Truckers now make about $70,000 a year on average. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said, 'There's never been a better time for America's former service members to get behind the wheel of a big rig.' Some immigrant groups say the crackdown unfairly targets certain communities, like Sikh drivers. But for now, the 'Freedom Haulers' are rolling out.
why_it_matters: If you see big trucks on the road, they might be carrying the snacks or toys you buy, and the drivers could be veterans who served in the military and are now keeping the country's supplies moving.

keywords.explanation: Freedom Haulers is the name of a government campaign to get veterans to become truck drivers.
Audits are careful checks to make sure rules are being followed.
A commercial driver's license is a special permit to drive big trucks for work.
The GI Bill is a U.S. program that pays for veterans' education or job training.
A crackdown is when the government gets very strict about enforcing a rule.
Sikhs are people who follow a religion from South Asia, and many work as truckers in the U.S.

background_read: Truck drivers are very important because they deliver food, medicine, and other goods across the country.
For many years, many truck drivers in the United States have come from other countries, especially from South Asia and Mexico.
The GI Bill has helped millions of veterans go to college or learn new skills since World War II.
Article_Structure: WHO: U.S. military veterans and the Transportation Department.
WHAT: The government started the 'Freedom Haulers' campaign to get veterans to replace immigrant truckers who lost their licenses.
WHERE: Across the United States, especially on highways where big trucks drive.
WHY: Because about 26,000 immigrant drivers failed English tests and 30,000 licenses were canceled after stricter checks.

perspectives.description: The government thinks this is a great way to give veterans well-paying jobs while keeping the economy running, since truckers are badly needed.
Some immigrant groups feel the strict English tests are unfair and target certain communities, like Sikhs, who have been driving trucks safely for a long time.
Trucking businesses just need enough drivers, whether they are veterans or immigrants, so they might not care who is behind the wheel as long as the goods get delivered.
